summary: Nikolayevsk-na-Amure Airport (NLI) is a regional airport serving the remote town of Nikolayevsk-na-Amure in Khabarovsk Krai, located in Russia's Far East near the mouth of the Amur River and the Sea of Okhotsk. The airport functions as a vital transportation link for this isolated community, which is otherwise difficult to reach due to limited road and rail infrastructure. It primarily handles domestic flights connecting residents to larger regional hubs.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Nikolayevsk-na-Amure Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional carriers operating domestic flights, most notably connecting to Khabarovsk and other Far Eastern Russian cities.

Q: How far is the airport from Nikolayevsk-na-Amure town center?
A: The airport is located a short distance from the town, typically reachable within about 15-20 minutes by car.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: No, Nikolayevsk-na-Amure Airport handles domestic flights only, serving regional routes within Russia's Far East.

Q: What is the best time to fly to this airport?
A: Summer months generally offer more reliable weather conditions, as winter in this northern region can bring significant snowfall and harsh conditions that may affect flight schedules.
transport_tips: Taxis and local marshrutka (minibus) services are the primary means of reaching the airport from Nikolayevsk-na-Amure. There is no rail service to the town, so air travel via NLI is often the most practical way to connect to major regional centers. Travelers should arrange ground transportation in advance, especially during winter months when services may be limited.
local_tip: Pack warm clothing even in summer — Nikolayevsk-na-Amure sits at a northern latitude near the Sea of Okhotsk and can experience surprisingly cool, foggy conditions influenced by cold coastal waters.
